text:
maria: heads up — we've got a reproducible tail-latency regression on multi-GPU pipeline/tensor-parallel runs when the job spans PCIe-only links. NVLink-only boxes are fine. p95 went from ~95ms to ~115-120ms for the same load. Can folks take a look? :thinking:

devin: what workload and model? can you drop the profile traces you collected?

maria: short repro with `stable-transformer-7b` on 4x A100 across two nodes (2 GPUs/node). seq_len ~1024, batch 2. Posted perf sample below (20s window):
```
# perf summary
p95 latency: 118ms
avg kernel compute: 42ms
avg comm windows: 30ms (spikes up to 70ms)
all-reduce overhead: ~18% of token time
PCIe throughput: periodic 8-9GB/s spikes
NVLink baseline: p95 96ms, all-reduce overhead ~9%
```

kenji: hmm — looks like the runtime is choosing a different attention/matmul kernel on the PCIe nodes. when comm windows expand we lose effective comm/compute overlap and the kin selection heuristic seems oblivious. could be the kernel latency model assumes NVLink bandwidth.

anya: also saw something similar earlier — KV-cache shard placement caused cross-node all-reduces to increase when some KV shards ended up on the remote PCIe endpoint. the extra round-trips hit when sequences have long prefixes.

devin: can you paste the timeline flame? i want to see if compute stalls waiting on recv or the kernel itself elongates.

maria: pasted a trimmed trace (annotated):
```
[0.00-0.12s] forward: fused-attn-kernel (good)
[0.12-0.18s] all-reduce (PCIe spike)
[0.18-0.25s] fallback matmul (higher latency)
[0.25-0.36s] KV fetch (cross-node) + wait
[repeat]
```

kenji: based on that: two issues in combination — (1) kernel selector picks unfused matmul when measured latency vs estimated bandwidth crosses threshold; (2) KV shard placement causes nonlocal fetches increasing comm windows. separately ok, together catastrophic.

kenji: quick patch idea — make kernelselect topology-aware and include a comm_overlap metric. pseudo: 
```
kernelselect:
  prefer_fused_if: seq_len < 1536
  fallback_thresholds:
    comm_overlap: 0.55  # if >0.55 prefer kernels that maximize compute/overlap
    bandwidth_factor: 0.8
```
small change, non-breaking, runtime will bias toward kernels that can hide repeat comm stalls.

anya: for KV: propose affinity change so KV shards colocate with tensor-parallel ranks when possible, avoid cross-node fetch for hot prefixes. Also add a lightweight sharding probe at startup to measure PCIe vs NVLink link quality and pin shards accordingly.

devin: ran a quick A/B on staging with both changes (kernelselect bias + KV affinity probe). numbers over 2k requests: 
```
control (current): p95 118ms, p99 205ms
A (kernelselect only): p95 105ms, p99 182ms
B (kernelselect + kv-affinity): p95 92ms, p99 145ms
cpu/gpu busy cycles reduced, PCIe spikes less frequent
```

maria: woah B looks promising. did you check correctness and memory footprint? any regressions in throughput?

devin: correctness fine (unit/e2e passed). memory up ~1.5% due to slight shard duplication during failover window, throughput same or slightly improved due to fewer stalls.

kenji: can we make the kernelselect change conservative? maybe use a sampling window and only switch at deploy time or via rollout flag. also add a perf counter exposing `comm_overlap_ratio` so we can alert when thresholds crossed.

anya: agree. i'll add the KV-affinity probe as opt-in via config `kv.affinity_probe: true` and default it off until we can monitor for side-effects.

maria: plan: 1) kenji will land conservative kernelselect bias behind feature flag; 2) anya will land kv-affinity_probe behind config; 3) devin will run canary (5% traffic) in us-east-1 on PCIe-backed pools, monitor p95/p99 + comm_overlap metric for 24h; 4) revert if p99 increases or error rate rises.

kenji: i'll open a tiny PR with comments and perf-counters instrumented. tag @devin for staging run. :thumbsup:

devin: staging canary started. command used to reproduce locally: 
```
./run_infer --model stable-transformer-7b --nodes 2 --gpus-per-node 2 --seq 1024 --batch 2 --trace perf.json
```

sre-bot: perf-alert 2067890400: us-east-1 pool PCIe nodes p95 increased above 110ms for model stable-transformer-7b — auto-notify sent.

maria: thanks all — good triage. after canary completes we'll decide rollout. saved traces in /mnt/prof/2067890001/ if anyone needs them.

devin: noting follow-ups: add `comm_overlap_ratio` to console (per-route) and create an eval harness to replay long-prefix workloads for future regressions.

anya: will prepare the KV-affinity config docs and tests.

maria: resolved for now. keep thread updated with canary metrics. :white_check_mark:
